title: Entropy-Bounded Empiricism: Core Principles
description: Foundational specification of Entropy-Bounded Empiricism (EBE), a regime-aware epistemic framework for interpreting measurements in entropy- and energy-flow-governed systems. It introduces the S-axis (physical regime hierarchy) and L-axis (epistemic layer hierarchy) and formalizes the Regime-Consistent Measurement Protocol (RCMP) to prevent regime leakage and interpretive overreach. The paper codifies regime gating and proxy-chain transparency to make assumptions traceable and claims comparable across regimes.

s_axis_regime_classification.description: Maps normalized entropy state to physical regime classes, establishing where different physical descriptions are appropriate.

l_axis_layers.description: Defines the epistemic layer hierarchy from minimally assumed measurements to fully model-dependent constructs.

layer_transparency_chain.description: Axiom of Layer Transparency: each step up the L-axis introduces assumptions that must be documented.

rcmp_coupling_rule.description: Anchors interpretation at the lowest epistemic layer that remains directly coupled to the physical driver for a given S-regime.

regime_gating_validity.latex: \mathrm{Validity}(M) = \{\, S \;|\; \text{primary variables of } M \text{ are driver-near in } S \,\}
regime_gating_validity.description: Formal statement of the Regime-Gating Principle: a model is epistemically valid only within regimes where its primary variables are driver-near.

proxy_chain_transparency.description: Proxy-chain decomposition from raw data (D) to calibrated observables (O), derived quantities (Q), and theoretical constructs (T), with explicit assumption sets A_i.

key_results.main_finding: EBE establishes a regime-aware mapping between physical entropy regimes (S-axis) and epistemic layers (L-axis) via RCMP, enforcing regime-gated interpretation and proxy-chain transparency to prevent interpretive overreach.

kill_criteria: KC1: Systematic cross-domain evidence that L3 (model-dependent) claims exhibit lower total uncertainty and higher out-of-sample predictive accuracy than L1/L2 for the same S-regime after full proxy-chain accounting, contradicting Principle 4.1 (Epistemic Degradation).

KC2: Verified cases where a model whose primary variables are not driver-near in a given S-regime consistently outperforms driver-near models across that regime without added assumption load, violating Principle 6.1 (Regime Gating).

KC3: Demonstration that bypassing RCMP anchoring (e.g., interpreting High-S phenomena primarily at L3 while skipping L1/L2) systematically yields more reliable and reproducible inferences than the RCMP-recommended L1/L2 anchoring across independent datasets, falsifying Definition 5.1/Principle 5.1.

KC4: Widespread reproducible findings that omission of documented assumption sets (A1–A3) has no measurable impact on interpretability, reproducibility, or uncertainty quantification across regimes, showing Proxy-Chain Transparency provides no epistemic benefit.

KC5: Identification of a single universal model whose primary variables remain driver-near and require no regime-specific recalibration across Low-S, Mid-S, and High-S domains while retaining stable performance, nullifying the need for S-axis regime partitioning.
